COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No.207 of 2021
Shri Vipin Sanghi, C.J.
Shri Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.
Mr. K. P. Upadhyay, learned Sr.
Counsel assisted by Mr. Hemant Pant,
learned counsel for the petitioners.
Mr. J. C. Pande, learned Standing
Counsel for the State.
Ms. Meena Bisht, learned counsel
holding brief of Mr. Yogesh Pacholia,
learned counsel for respondent no.3.
Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, learned counsel for
respondent no.5.
The petitioners have preferred the
present petition to seek the following
reliefs:-
"a) issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari calling for the records
and quashing the annexure -1
communication dated 06.01.2021 issued by
the 3rd respondent National Council for
Teacher Education as well as the subsequent
annexure -2 order dated 15.01.2021 issued
by the Secretary, Education, Uttarakhand
Govt. whereby the selection criterion for the
post of Assistant Teacher in Govt. Primary
Schools is being varied in the midst of the
selection process.
b) issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing and holding
that the 18-month online Diploma Course in
Elementary Education of National Institute of
Open Schooling, Noida (U.P.) for un-trained
in-service teachers working in Govt./Govt.
Aided/Un aided Private Schools, cannot be
treated at par with the two-year regular
Diploma Course in Elementary Education
conducted by the District Institutes of
Education and Training in the State of
Uttarakhand in absence of any law made
therefor.
c) issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing and

2
commanding the State respondents to
conclude the ongoing selection process
strictly in accordance with the Uttarakhand
Govt. Elementary Education (Teacher)
Service Rules, 2012 as amended upto
29.07.2019 read with the provisions of the
Right of Children to Fee and Compulsory
Education Act, 2009 and the National Council
for Teacher Education Act, 1993."
We have already rendered our
judgment in batch of writ petitions
including the WPSS No. 350 of 2021 dated
14.09.2022.
In light of the said judgment the
present petition is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, we dismiss the present
writ petition.
(R.C. Khulbe, J.) (Vipin Sanghi, C.J.)
 29.09.2022
